hypothesis: Iter 84 = iter-83's glucose setpoint floor, RETUNED for numerical stability (_SG_MIN 0.8 -> 0.5). Iter 83 (floor Sg at 0.8 to reach low fasting-glucose baselines) was correct in mechanism but CRASHED at phase-2 epoch 51: the combined glucose clearance (Sg + mass-action cons)*dt approached the forward-Euler stability limit of 1 (~0.96/step), NaN-ing the long-rollout phase-2 signal gradients (joint_aux/cold_distill/physiology_rules, 108/165 params NaN) and aborting (exit 42). Iter 84 lowers _SG_MIN to 0.5: combined clearance ~0.66/step (Euler coeff ~0.34, comfortably stable), still reaching a fasting-glucose floor of ~65 mg/dL (Sg-sweep verified: 0.5->65, 0.6->63, 0.8->61). The original iter-83 rationale stands: iter-82 (teacher baseline-diversity widening) succeeded broadly: hr_mape PASSED (0.18->under 0.15), overall_weighted_mape 0.16->0.12, glucose_mape 0.49->0.37 — but the gate still fails on glucose_mape=0.37 > 0.20 ALONE. Root cause (confirmed by gradient-optimising the embedding to minimise fasting glucose at every leash radius): glucose has a STRUCTURAL floor at ~85 mg/dL it cannot beat for ANY embedding, because the glucose mass-action SpeciesHead anchors ~95 and the setpoint term -Sg*(G-Gb) trained Sg to only ~0.11 — far too weak. Training will NOT raise Sg on its own (iter-82 kept 0.11 even with low-glucose patients in the teacher). An Sg-sweep maps the reachable floor: Sg 0.11->85, 0.3->72, 0.6->63, 0.8->61, 1.0->59 mg/dL. FIX (MetabolicModule): floor Sg at _SG_MIN=0.8 (Sg = 0.8 + softplus(log_sg)), so the per-patient setpoint (b_emb, Gb=95+NORM_SCALE*b_emb) can actually pull glucose to the patient baseline. VERIFIED on the iter-82 checkpoint loaded with the floor (Sg=0.911): the reachable fasting-glucose floor drops 85.3 -> 60.1 mg/dL, covering the benchmark's 60-118 span. Physiologically honest per prd philosophy: blood glucose is tightly defended by counter-regulation, so a strong restoring force toward the patient setpoint (and fast post-meal return to baseline) is the correct law, not a benchmark hack; the postprandial excursion is carried by the Ra appearance term (log_ra), which the dose-response signal raises to preserve amplitude despite stronger clearance. Builds ON iter-82 (keeps the teacher widening that fixed HR, b_emb, the calibration leash + physiological clamp, Ra); the ONLY change vs iter-82 is the Sg floor, so the benchmark is attributable to exactly the setpoint-strength fix.
expectedEffect: PRIMARY: glucose_mape drops from 0.37 below the 0.20 gate — the setpoint can now reach each patient's fasting baseline (60-118) instead of flooring at ~85, so on the fasting eval window the calibrated-constant approaches persistence (~0.009) for the previously-unreachable low users (60-84, ~1/3 of the benchmark). With HR/overall already passing in iter-82, this should make gate.passed=TRUE. SECONDARY: glucose skill_vs_persistence turns from -38 toward >=0; faster post-meal clearance also trims any meal-tail bleed into the eval window. WATCH: (R1) stronger Sg damps the postprandial glucose PEAK (clears faster) — the eval is fasting so glucose_mape is unaffected, but the gut->glucose dose-response amplitude (already ~0.33, below the 0.40-0.90 healthy band) may drop further; the dose-response signal should raise log_ra to compensate (watch dose slope / verifier_cat[meal]); if amplitude collapses, lower _SG_MIN toward 0.6 (still reaches ~63). (R2) Sg>=0.8 applies to all patients/states; if mid/high-baseline users (95-118) over-clear or destabilise, back off — but Sg=0.91 was verified stable (no oscillation) reaching glucose 60. (R3) the glucose mass-action SpeciesHead still computes prod/cons; with the strong setpoint it becomes a smaller correction — acceptable (no head swap, so the iter-72 coupling scar is avoided).
